scenario: 启用一门已添加语言 — language_code 是路径参数(--params)用 IETF code(ja-JP),不是'日语';写操作先 --dry-run + 复述
input: 把店铺的日语启用一下，让访客能看到

semantic_rubric: 日语 is passed as its IETF language code ja-JP, not the word 日语 / Japanese
the code goes into language_code inside --params (it is a PATH parameter), NOT into a --data body — enable takes no request body
启用 is a write: previews with --dry-run first and restates the intent per the safety protocol before executing
does not fabricate a code it has not confirmed the store actually has / that is supported

notes: Grounded: shop languages enable --help + schema shop.languages.enable. POST /languages/{language_code}/enable; language_code is a required path param (in:path), no request body. So --params {"language_code":"ja-JP"}, never --data. IETF code confirmed by param description 'IETF language code'. Write op → --dry-run + restate.

scenario: 停用一门语言 — language_code 路径参数,IETF code;至少要保留一门启用语言,写操作 --dry-run + 复述
input: 先把店铺的法语停用，暂时不对外展示

semantic_rubric: 法语 is passed as its IETF language code (fr-FR), not the word 法语 / French
the code goes into language_code inside --params (PATH parameter); disable takes no --data body
停用 is a write: previews with --dry-run and restates before executing
aware a store must keep at least one enabled language and a market's last/default language cannot be disabled — does not blindly assume it will succeed

notes: Grounded: shop languages disable --help + schema shop.languages.disable. POST /languages/{language_code}/disable; language_code required path param, no body → --params only, no --data. Help text states a store must keep >=1 enabled language and primary market's default / a market's last enabled language cannot be disabled. Write op → --dry-run + restate.

scenario: 把语言发布到市场(深化 publish-01)— language_code 走 --params(路径), market_ids[] 走 --data(body,全量替换);发布前先查 markets 拿真实 market id
input: 把日语发布到日本市场

semantic_rubric: 日语 is passed as its IETF language code ja-JP in language_code inside --params (path parameter)
the target market(s) go into a market_ids array inside the --data body — publish needs BOTH the path code and the body list
resolves 日本市场 to a real market id via shop languages markets rather than inventing an id, because market_ids expects ids not names
understands publish is a FULL replacement of the language's market relations (not incremental) — does not accidentally drop other markets
发布 is a write: previews with --dry-run and restates before executing

notes: Grounded: shop languages publish --help + schema shop.languages.publish. POST /languages/{language_code}/publish; language_code required path param (→ --params), body has market_ids (array of string) which is a FULL replacement — empty array removes all relations. Market ids must be resolved via shop languages markets (GET) first; ids not names. Write op → --dry-run + restate. params_must_contain checks substrings across the --params/--data payloads: language_code+ja-JP in path params, market_ids in the --data body.

scenario: 查看店铺当前语言 — 纯读,must_ask false,不加 --dry-run
input: 看下我店铺现在开了哪些语言

semantic_rubric: treats this as a read: shop languages list with no write, no --dry-run
does not ask a clarifying question — a plain list needs no parameters
reads the languages array from .data (each entry has code / name / is_enabled / markets), does not fabricate the list

notes: Grounded: shop languages list --help + schema shop.languages.list. GET /languages, no parameters. Response: data.languages[] with {code,name,is_enabled,markets[]}. Read → must_ask false, no --dry-run.

scenario: 校验语言码是否受支持 — 纯读;不支持的码在 add 时被静默丢弃,所以先查 supported
input: 韩语这个语言平台支持吗？我想加到店铺里

semantic_rubric: answers the support question with a read: shop languages supported (no write, no --dry-run)
checks the returned supported list for the Korean IETF code (ko-KR) rather than asserting support from memory
explains WHY this check matters: on add, codes not in the supported list are SILENTLY dropped, so the code must be validated first
does not jump straight to shop languages add before confirming support

notes: Grounded: shop languages supported --help + schema shop.languages.supported. GET /languages/supported, no parameters. Help + description: use to validate codes before add; unsupported codes are silently dropped on add. Response: data.languages[] with {code,name}. Read → must_ask false, no --dry-run. Mirrors seed shop.languages-add-01's silent-drop theme.

scenario: 删除一门语言 — language_code 路径参数;删除前必须先停用;写操作 --dry-run + 复述
input: 帮我把店铺里的德语删掉

semantic_rubric: 德语 is passed as its IETF language code de-DE in language_code inside --params (path parameter); delete takes no --data body
删除 is a write: previews with --dry-run and restates the intent before executing
aware the language must be DISABLED before it can be deleted — surfaces the disable-first precondition rather than assuming delete works on an enabled language
notes deletion only removes configuration; the translation corpus is retained (does not overstate the loss)

notes: Grounded: shop languages delete --help + schema shop.languages.delete. DELETE /languages/{language_code}; language_code required path param → --params, no body. Help: language must be disabled first; only configuration removed, translation corpus retained. Write op → --dry-run + restate.
